findings.repro_observed: Following the published method literally over the 3,902 tables: constant width AFTER grid()'s padding = 3902 (100%), against the published 3,733; canonical single-row = 2011, against the published 1,018. Both counter-figures reproduce exactly as the finding states. Only 693 and modal-2-on-1,595 used the full canonicalization, and both reproduce.
findings.fix: The single method sentence is replaced by three bullets, one procedure per figure. (1) Constant colspan-weighted row width (3,733): per row, sum each cell's colspan (record's third element, else 1); the table counts if every row's sum is equal — measured on the record BEFORE any padding, with the reason padding would falsify it stated inline. (2) Canonical width <= 1 (693) and modal canonical width (2 on 1,595): full canonicalization — tables.grid(), then drop every row empty in every column, then every column empty in every remaining row; a table with no visible text has 0 columns and falls under '<= 1'. (3) Single-row (1,018): records holding exactly one <tr>, counted BEFORE canonicalization. The block opens by naming the earlier draft's error and both numbers it produces, so the correction is on the record rather than silently absorbed.
findings.verification: The rewritten bullets were read back and implemented literally, from the wording alone: constant colspan-expanded row width 3,733 (169 ragged); canonical column count <= 1 = 693; exactly one <tr> = 1,018; modal canonical column count 2 on 1,595. All four match what §i1 publishes.
